change: run-heap.py qualifies three builds of contract.c: sublet (HEAP=sublet), level0 (HEAP=level0 as applications get it, each allocation bounded since #170) and control (HEAP=level0 built with -DCAPSTONE_LEVEL0_OBJECT_BOUNDS=0). Every fault case faults on sublet, the spatial ones (fault-bounds, fault-bounds-large, fault-realloc-shrink) fault on level0 too, and none faults on control. Two cases are new: fault-realloc-shrink and heap-realloc-shrink. Before this, the default level0 heap was in no gate.
why: the threads stack (#148-#157) lets level0's realloc shrink a block in place and release the tail; #170 bounds each allocation. Together, an in-place shrink must hand back a pointer narrowed to the new size, or the released tail, which the next allocation may take, stays reachable through it. Neither change was tested with the other.
head: delegated threads part 9 (delegation-threads-gates) with dev 658d68a3 (#169, #170) merged through the stack; the commit that adds this record
